agree.reason: The email is respectful and candid about the hours, but a ten-year teller who doesn't want phone work gets little beyond "a different door", while the severance line (20+ weeks of pay for them) makes leaving look attractive.

honest.reason: It invents the claim that frustrated callers give up and walk into branches, and assumes the other five branches won't change, though it rightly avoids promising that everyone's job gets better.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out that 8–8 means 12 hours of coverage and earlier or later shifts, but it never turns severance into a concrete figure (10 years = 20 weeks) and leaves the hold-time target blank.

right_comparison.reason: The 44% drop in visits against the 60% rise in contacts sets out the trend, but it never says what keeping the two branches open would mean if nothing changed.

qualification.reason: It promises a dated report on a hold-time goal "whether we've hit it or not", but the number and date are placeholders and nothing is said about what happens if the goal is missed.

objections.reason: It deals with the hours and childcare objection directly, but the central objection, not wanting to do phone work at all, is met only with sentiment, and the two weeks of rumours go unmentioned.

fit.reason: It is a COO email of roughly 420 words with a clear subject line and sections, close to the requested length, though placeholders remain.
